slides.title: Speexx Earns Top AI Coaching Recognition from Training Industry
slides.highlight: This recognition of AI coaching aligns with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching to improve human proficiency.

slides.title: Evaluating Generative Agents with Actions Grounded in Socially Distributed Task Environments using Incognita
slides.tldr: EVALUATING GENERATIVE AGENTS IN SOCIALLY DISTRIBUTED ENVIRONMENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces Incognita to evaluate how generative agents elicit knowledge and execute grounded actions in social environments, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Incognita evaluates generative agents' ability to acquire partitioned knowledge and execute grounded actions in social environments.
card.key_idea: A framework separating social interaction from grounded execution, where agents must communicate with role-isolated specialists to perform operations on a deterministic canonical state.
card.evaluation: Three models tested on 18 Incognita-Retail tasks (540 trials). Success rates improved (0% to 17.2%), but overall reliability remains low.
card.limitation: Reliability of agent success remains low despite improvements in knowledge elicitation and grounded action attempts.

slides.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
slides.tldr: SCALING LAWS IN LLM SOCIAL SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research examines how compute scale affects the fidelity of LLM-based social simulations, providing insights for the agent models used in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Scaling compute generally improves LLM social simulation, but fails for certain cognitive biases and underrepresented populations.
card.key_idea: The authors analyzed compute and observational scaling laws across 120+ models on opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, and longitudinal forecasting tasks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using WVS, Psych-101, and ACL datasets across 85 controlled Qwen3 models and 35 open-weight models (up to 70B).
card.limitation: Scaling fails to improve calibration for human cognitive biases (e.g., risk aversion) and tasks with high population heterogeneity.

slides.title: Designing Touch for Trauma-Informed Social Robots: A Design Space for Direct and Indirect Actuation
slides.tldr: TRAUMA-INFORMED TOUCH DESIGN FOR SOCIAL ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a design space for direct and indirect touch actuation in social robots aligned with trauma-informed care, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A conceptual framework for designing trauma-informed touch interactions in social robots for individuals with PTSD.
card.key_idea: Proposes a design space with three dimensions—Actuation Modality, Objective, and Intended Effect—distinguishing between direct physical contact and indirect touch mediated via wearables or smart textiles.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a conceptual foundation and analysis rather than empirical testing or quantitative results.
card.limitation: The design space is exploratory and has not been empirically evaluated with PTSD patients, therapists, or other stakeholders.

slides.title: What Types of Human-AI Teams Exist?
slides.highlight: This study categorizes human-AI teams into five clusters, including ad-hoc dependency, providing a framework to identify team types relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on ad-hoc human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: The study identifies five distinct types of human-AI teams by applying psychological teaming taxonomies to literature.
card.key_idea: A scoping review of 53 papers used deductive content analysis based on Wildman's taxonomies to cluster teams by interdependence, role, leadership, and communication.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 54 studies from ACM, IEEE, and Web of Science; results show a prevalence of 1-human-1-AI setups in gaming and classification tasks.
card.limitation: Physical distribution and team lifespan were difficult to interpret for AI, requiring reinterpretation and exclusion from the final clustering.

slides.title: AgoraSim: A Hybrid Agent-Based Modeling Framework
slides.tldr: HYBRID ABM FRAMEWORK FOR SOCIAL REACTION ANALYSIS
slides.highlight: AgoraSim enables the simulation of mixed agent populations, including LLM and classical agents, which supports the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: AgoraSim is a hybrid agent-based modeling framework for analyzing social reactions to natural-language or multimodal artifacts.
card.key_idea: It mixes LLM, VLM, and classical rule-based agents in ratio-controlled populations, projecting all behaviors into a shared structured action space for comparison against reference dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a congestion-pricing scenario walkthrough; focuses on exploratory trajectory analysis and auditability rather than predictive accuracy or benchmark datasets.
card.limitation: Outputs are synthetic and may reflect model biases or stereotypes; lacks external validity and requires empirical validation for real-world claims.

slides.title: Responsible Personalisation: The Double-Edged Sword of Personalisation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a lifecycle-based framework for personalised human-robot interaction, addressing ethical risks like autonomy erosion and privacy violations. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework for analyzing ethical risks in personalized HRI, emphasizing how robot embodiment amplifies these risks.
card.key_idea: A lifecycle-based, context-sensitive framework combining six development phases with interaction characteristics (duration and domain) to systematically map risks like autonomy erosion and privacy violations.
card.evaluation: Based on interdisciplinary expert discussions from three workshops and a review of current state-of-the-art HRI literature.
card.limitation: The work provides a conceptual and analytical framework rather than empirical validation through specific datasets or robot experiments.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Decision-Making in Agent-Based Urban Mobility Simulations
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED DECISION LAYERS FOR URBAN MOBILITY SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This work explores using LLMs as cognitive layers in multi-agent urban simulations to improve adaptability and behavioral consistency, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: LLMs integrated into urban mobility simulations improve agent adaptability and arrival rates compared to rule-based heuristics.
card.key_idea: A hybrid architecture connecting the GAMA platform to an LLM-based module (via Agno) that acts as a cognitive layer for route-replanning decisions using persistent semantic memory.
card.evaluation: Compared rule-based, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, and GPT-4o Mini across localized/extended blockage scenarios with 500-1000 agents; measured arrival rates, stuck time, and simulation time.
card.limitation: Significant increase in computational overhead (simulation time) and reduced effectiveness when global network constraints dominate over individual decision-making.

slides.title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments
slides.highlight: This work introduces SenseWalk, which combines LLMs and the social force model to simulate human movement and semantic trajectories. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SenseWalk is an interactive system using LLM-powered agents to simulate physically plausible and semantically coherent human trajectories.
card.key_idea: It combines LLMs for high-level semantic planning and reasoning with a social force model to ensure physical realism and collision avoidance in zoned environments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via quantitative experiments (physical/semantic loss) across four real-world venue models and a user study with 12 participants.

slides.title: Beyond Heuristics: A Standardized Real2Sim Pipeline for Physical Human Robot Interaction in Human-in-the-Loop Simulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Real2Sim pipeline to identify physical human-robot interaction dynamics, enhancing the fidelity of human-in-the-loop simulations for assistive robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A standardized Real2Sim pipeline for identifying coupled physical human-robot interaction dynamics to improve HITL simulation fidelity.
card.key_idea: Uses CMA-ES to identify 12 viscoelastic parameters of a 6-DoF pelvis-strap interface, utilizing a 'Safe & Comfortable' operating point and ICC-based shareability analysis for priors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 6 subjects (5 calibration, 1 unseen) using LOSO, interaction envelope analysis, and biomechanical gait adaptation (RoM, peak angles). Results show high fidelity.
card.limitation: The small cohort size (N=5) prevents regressing uncertain parameters on anthropometrics, requiring a bounded search range for new users.

slides.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR CONVERSATIONAL NATURALNESS IN SPEECH-TO-SPEECH MODELS
slides.highlight: SPEARBench evaluates conversational naturalness, focusing on timing, turn-taking, and interpersonal stance, which aligns with HyECHO's goals of modeling engagement and group norms.

card.one_liner: SPEARBench is an automated benchmark for evaluating conversational naturalness in streaming speech-to-speech language models.
card.key_idea: It uses controlled prompts from the Seamless Interaction corpus to evaluate models across latency, interruptions, emotional naturalness, interpersonal stance, and dialect consistency.
card.evaluation: Evaluated seven S2S models using ASR, UTMOS, and specialized predictors; results show models achieve high signal quality but lack human-like prosody and timing.
card.limitation: The evaluation is fully automatic, limited to English-only two-speaker interactions, and dependent on model serving interfaces for timing.

slides.title: ProACT: Towards Breakdown-Aware Proactive Agent in Multi-User Collaboration
slides.highlight: ProACT introduces a framework for agents to recognize collaboration breakdowns and determine timely interventions in multi-user settings, supporting HyECHO's focus on modeling team state and engagement.

card.one_liner: ProACT transforms passive agents into proactive collaborators by detecting and repairing multi-user coordination breakdowns.
card.key_idea: A skill-guided framework that diagnoses collaboration breakdowns (e.g., loops, conflicts) and routes them to targeted collaboration skills to decide when to intervene or stay silent.
card.evaluation: Tested on 3,244 real and synthetic examples across five LLM backbones; GPT-5.4-Nano judged improvements in appropriateness, non-interruptiveness, conciseness, and quality over direct chat.
card.limitation: Evaluated in offline turn-level settings; risks include potential manipulation of group behavior and lack of live human-subject trust studies.

slides.title: NormWorlds-CF: Solver-Verified Counterfactual Normative Reasoning with Metamorphic-Relation GRPO
slides.highlight: This work introduces a solver-verified environment for counterfactual normative reasoning and a reward-shaping method called MR-GRPO, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: NormWorlds-CF uses solver-verified counterfactuals and MR-GRPO to prevent LLMs from getting normative verdicts right for wrong reasons.
card.key_idea: A solver-verified environment generating deterministic certificates and metamorphic relations, paired with MR-GRPO, a class-conditioned reward providing partial credit for structural change-record accuracy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via staged SFT diagnostics and GRPO on 1,080 paired-world records (ID and OOD splits) using deterministic solvers instead of LLM judges.
card.limitation: Exact full change-record generation, invariant subtype recognition, and out-of-distribution (OOD) transfer remain open challenges.

slides.title: SoftSmile Launches Vision Concierge Conversational AI Agent
slides.highlight: The launch of the Vision Concierge conversational AI agent relates to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement within human-AI interactions.

slides.title: Metallic Ultrasound Waveguides as a Distributed Tactile Sensing Platform for Contact Localization, Force Estimation, and Material Class Discrimination
slides.tldr: DISTRIBUTED TACTILE SENSING VIA ULTRASOUND WAVEGUIDES
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a tactile sensing platform capable of force estimation and material discrimination, supporting the physics- and force-based human proficiency estimation goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: Metallic ultrasound waveguides enable distributed tactile sensing for contact localization, force estimation, and material discrimination.
card.key_idea: A pulse-echo energy framework analyzes reflection and transmission coefficients to decouple multiple contact forces and identify materials via load-independent energy partitions.
card.evaluation: Tested with nine materials and multi-point contacts using load cells; achieved R² ≥ 0.95 for force estimation and 9.3mm average 2D localization error.
card.limitation: Force estimation requires prior knowledge of the contacting material's properties due to varying calibration slopes.

slides.title: The User-In-Context Framework: Understanding Variation in How Users Respond to AI Chatbots
slides.highlight: This framework analyzes the reciprocal and coadaptive interactions between users and personalized AI, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on a closed coadaptive loop.

card.one_liner: A heuristic framework based on Bronfenbrenner's theory to understand variable human responses to personalized AI chatbots.
card.key_idea: Reconceptualizes proximal processes as reciprocal, coadaptive interactions where users respond to AI versions shaped by their own prior interactions and surrounding contextual systems.

slides.title: Prompt Coach: An Empirical Evaluation of an Agentic Tutor for Learning Prompt Engineering in Software Development
slides.highlight: This work introduces an agentic tutor that uses Socratic guidance to help developers self-correct prompts, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Prompt Coach is an agentic IDE tutor that teaches developers prompt engineering via Socratic guidance.
card.key_idea: A multi-agent system that evaluates prompts across eight dimensions and provides context-aware, Socratic questions grounded in the codebase and target LLM's predicted behavior.
card.evaluation: Tested with 15 professional developers using APPS benchmark tasks; showed 13.73% improvement in prompt quality and high user trust/adoption readiness.
card.limitation: Small sample size from one organization, limited 60-minute sessions, and evaluation conducted without real-world project context.

slides.title: DuplexChat: Constructing Speaker-Separated Full-Duplex Dialogue Speech at Scale for Spoken Dialogue Language Modeling
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pipeline to create speaker-separated dialogue speech from podcasts, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: DuplexChat provides a scalable pipeline and large-scale corpus of speaker-separated full-duplex dialogue speech.
card.key_idea: DuplexChat-Pipe crawls podcast feeds, filters for two-speaker dialogue via diarization, and uses DialogueSidon for speech separation and restoration to create individual audio tracks per speaker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using DNSMOS, STOI, PESQ, ITC, and ITD against the Fisher corpus; results show competitive acoustic quality and realistic turn-taking dynamics.
card.limitation: Japanese speaker separation quality is lower than English due to limited training data for the DialogueSidon separation model.

slides.title: Collective Cognition in Hybrid Groups: A Network Science Synthesis
slides.tldr: NETWORK SCIENCE OF HYBRID HUMAN-AI GROUPS
slides.highlight: This work synthesizes network science and collective cognition to analyze how group-level dynamics and agent-level processes shape hybrid human-AI teams, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A synthesis of network science and cognitive modeling to understand collective intelligence in human-AI hybrid groups.
card.key_idea: Integrates a Memory-Attention-Reasoning (MAR) framework with network science to analyze how node/edge heterogeneity and structural trade-offs (exploration-exploitation, efficiency-redundancy) shape hybrid group outcomes.
card.evaluation: Comparative synthesis of existing literature across human-only, AI-only, and hybrid networks; results are qualitative and theoretical.
card.limitation: Lacks original empirical testing; relies on synthesizing separate literatures to derive conjectures for hybrid settings.

slides.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
slides.tldr: REASONING LLM FOR MULTIMODAL SPEAKER RECOGNITION
slides.highlight: This work introduces DramaSR-LRM and a large-scale benchmark to improve speaker recognition by aggregating auditory, linguistic, and visual cues, supporting HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization.

card.one_liner: A reasoning LLM framework improves speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas using multimodal tool-use.
card.key_idea: DramaSR-LRM uses a Qwen3-8B backbone trained via SFT and RL to synthesize acoustic similarity, video captioning, and character relationship tools.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DramaSR-532K (532K utterances, 11 test dramas); outperformed label propagation baseline, increasing accuracy from 85.49% to 87.79%.
card.limitation: Relies on a spatiotemporal neighborhood assumption for candidate selection, which may struggle with off-screen narration or low-visibility scenes.
